FILES: client/src/research/assisted-order/api.ts, client/src/research/assisted-order/AssistedOrderCta.tsx, client/src/research/early-access/EarlyAccessRoute.storefront.test.tsx (beforeEach reset), vitest.config.ts. TESTS: client/src 188 files / 1802 tests ALL PASS; tsc clean. READ THIS BEFORE YOU CUT THE RC - TWO THINGS. (1) FALSE RED ON YOUR STOREFRONT GATE. vitest.config.ts had no css override, so vitest fell back to postcss.config.js which lists tailwindcss as a direct PostCSS plugin; Tailwind v4 moved that and THROWS. Any test transitively importing a .css file died with a PostCSS error instead of a test result. vite.config.ts already neutralizes it identically, which is why npm run build was fine and this stayed hidden. It presented as ORDER DEPENDENCE: EarlyAccessRoute.storefront.test.tsx - the test that proves the unified storefront - PASSES in a full-directory run and FAILS run alone. Any worker verifying the storefront on its own file saw red on green code. Fixed here. I touched vitest.config.ts, which is shared infra - please review that one line; it can only turn a throw into a no-op, since no assertion can depend on a pipeline that never succeeded. (2) CLIENT-SIDE CATALOG LATENCY, MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER. Three components fetch assisted-orders/config independently (route bridge probe, CTA, wizard), and they are SEQUENTIAL because the wizard only mounts after the route probe resolves. Against a stub answering in ~10ms the catalog request still did not START until 2553ms: config -> lazy chunk -> config again -> catalog. On mobile each hop is a full cellular RTT stacked in front of the expensive request. Now one shared in-flight promise; rejections not cached so a failed probe stays retryable. THIS IS NOT THE 30-60s FIX - that is server-side query cost - it removes the client latency stacked in front of it. I could not measure the real server: the production bundle cannot boot in a worker session without Supabase service creds (pre-existing; scripts/preview-research.mjs fails identically), so my browser proof runs the REAL built client against stubbed doors. Someone with working credentials must measure the actual catalog endpoint against the founder's targets. EARLIER SLICE: 543b0461 (origin-verified) undid my duplicate Featured/All - the route already had it at 6eef533; I kept the scope-safety proof and the quantity-copy fix. Note I have nothing asserting the old $49/$59 prices anywhere.
